subject: Overnight cutover coverage question — SOC 2 Type II reporting period
messages:
From: Jamie Lin <jamie.lin@acme-corp.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 22:15:00 -0700
Subject: Question on SOC 2 period — overnight migration on 2026-12-31

Hi Irene,

Quick question from our audit team as we finalize our SOC 2 assessment for Acme: we have a scheduled platform migration that occurred on 2026-12-31 and the cutover window spans 23:45 local time to 00:15 local time (overnight). For your SOC 2 Type II report covering 2026, can you confirm whether events that happened during that partial-day cutover are considered within the report period (i.e., are logs, change manifests and control evidence for the 12/31 local-day included up to the local-day end, or up to UTC midnight)?

Specifically:
- Is the reporting cutoff inclusive of 2026-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, or is it based on Redwood local-time boundaries?
- If any evidence hangs on a migration that completed after UTC midnight, do you provide a bridge letter or other attestation for that transitional window?

We may need a short bridge letter for the audit if the coverage differs. Can you advise and, if necessary, provide the estimated turnaround for a letter and the signatory?

Thanks — Jamie (on behalf of SFO Audit)
SFO Audit Team
Acme Corp

Thanks for the clear summary — copying our compliance and audit lead (Marissa) and controls owner (Karthik) to confirm the exact cutover treatment. We understand the cutover spanned 23:45 local time into the next calendar day; please confirm the local timezone used (PDT / PST / other) and whether the in-flight events you mention involve configuration pushes, data migrations, or both. That will help our evidence pull.

Tentatively: we generally consider the SOC 2 Type II reporting period inclusive through 23:59:59 UTC on the period end date, but there are nuances for migrations that cross the UTC midnight boundary (especially for manifests produced post-cutover). Marissa — can you confirm our standard language and whether a bridge letter will be required in this scenario? If a bridge letter is appropriate, we can draft and sign within 2 business days; let me know the preferred signatory (Head of Security vs. VP Compliance) — Jamie, any preference on your side?

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>

Subject: Re: Question on SOC 2 period — overnight migration on 2026-12-31

Irene / Karthik — thanks for looping me in. Jamie — hi, quick summary below and proposed next steps.

Short answer: Redwood's SOC 2 Type II report for calendar-year 2026 treats the reporting window as inclusive through 2026-12-31 23:59:59 UTC. In practice that means:
- Control evidence and system logs timestamped on or before 2026-12-31 23:59:59 UTC are considered part of the period.
- Events that completed after 23:59:59 UTC fall outside the certified period unless there is explicit attestational language (bridge letter) stating otherwise.

Notes on cutovers/migrations that cross UTC midnight:
- For migrations that start before UTC midnight and finish after, we will include the pre-cutover evidence and any generated artifacts whose timestamps are within the period (e.g., change manifests stamped 2026-12-31T23:55:00Z).
- If the finalization or reconciliation steps produced artifacts with timestamps after 2026-12-31T23:59:59Z, those artifacts are technically outside the period.

Bridge letter guidance:
- We can provide a short bridge letter that explicitly confirms the timeline of the cutover and whether specific reconciliation artifacts were created post-cutoff and how they were handled.
- Typical turnaround is 1–2 business days to draft, plus up to 2 business days for signature routing.
- Standard signatory: VP, Compliance & Audit (we can escalate to Head of Security on request).

Deliverables we can produce for your audit package on request:
- Draft bridge letter (PDF) that references the migration times and the reporter signatory.
- A CSV manifest of reconciliation logs and timestamps for 2026-12-31 (we will redact internal hostnames on request).
- Copy of the SOC 2 Type II report (reference attached).

If you confirm the local timezone (PDT/PST) and whether you want the bridge letter to state coverage for the entire migration window (23:45 local to 00:15 local), I'll:
1) Prepare the bridge letter draft and a redacted log manifest (log_manifest_2026-12-31.csv).
2) Put the draft through our internal signatory flow and share a PDF and DocuSign link.

Marissa Cole

Thanks, Marissa — that helps a lot.

Confirming: the migration was in PDT and the window we care about is 2026-12-31 23:45 PST through 2027-01-01 00:15 PST (so some artifacts are after UTC midnight). Acme requests a bridge letter that:
- Confirms Redwood's SOC 2 reporting cutoff (2026-12-31 23:59:59 UTC).
- Explicitly states whether reconciliation artifacts time-stamped after that cutoff were produced and whether those artifacts affect the controls in scope.
- Is signed by Head of Security or VP, Compliance & Audit.

Please proceed with the draft bridge letter and redacted manifest. Prefer Head of Security signatory if that's available within the 2-business-day window.

If you can share a DocuSign link once the draft is ready, we'll route internally and include the PDF in our audit binder.

Thanks — Jamie
SFO Audit, Acme Corp
